## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag has to take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, as the project's CLI flag rules require for every new flag under `cli/`. That policy gap is the only defect this review found, and it should be fixed.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option. `collect` now skips any file whose basename matches one of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The pull request also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds tests for parsing, filtering and the archive that `main` writes.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'`, nothing is excluded, because `default=[]` never reads the environment. This breaks the rule at `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that pass options through the environment cannot use `--exclude`, so files they intend to skip still end up in the archive. — Fix: Split `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE", "")` on a documented separator to build the default list, add the variable to `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the environment case.
